answer: At the identity summit, each agent must post a bond whose size is set by a Paris-law crack-growth model, so forged identities are costly seeds that propagate under repeated challenge cycles. Every registration quill signs a growth-rate exponent m≈3, letting the registry predict how many cheap sybils an attacker can sustain before cumulative bond loss exceeds forgery cost. The limit is a walnut of residual risk: attackers who accept slow, low-amplitude identity churn stay below detection, so thresholds must be recalibrated as load spectra shift.
